children: The National Stock Exchange of India has cut the size of its long-awaited IPO by more than 15% and will take investor orders next week, its prospectus showed on Thursday.

The offering, expected to be one of India's largest, comes after years of delays and at a time when India's IPO market regains momentum, paving the way for a fresh wave of marquee listings, including billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio.
NSE's IPO ‌will be an offer for sale with no fresh capital raised, where existing investors including State Bank of India
, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and General Insurance Corporation of India
will offload 126.4 million shares, down from the 148.91 million planned earlier, with SBI selling the most shares.
NSE's share sale will open for subscription on September 17 and close on September 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for September 16, the bourse said in a filing.
Shares will likely be priced between 1,700 rupees and 1,785 rupees apiece, Reuters reported on Wednesday.
NSE, the country's biggest exchange by trading volumes, dominates the derivatives market and has benefited from a surge in retail trading in the world's most populous country.

NSE's revenue from operations stood at 166 billion rupees ($1.74 billion) for the year ended March, with a profit of 103.02 billion rupees. The bourse had 129.09 million registered investors and 2,978 listed entities.
